A cube is expanding uniformly at a rate of $57{\text{ cm}}^{3}\text{/s}.$ How fast is each edge of the cube increasing when the volume of the cube is $27{\text{ cm}}^{3}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the cube and let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=57\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ when $V=27\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the cube:

$$
V={x}^{3}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Before we plug in the known values, we need to find the value of $x$ when $V=27\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={x}^{3} \\ 27 & ={x}^{3} \\ x & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug $x=3$ and $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=57$ into the expression for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ 57 & =3(3)^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\, \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{19}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sides of the cube are increasing at a rate of $\frac{19}{9}\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ at the moment when $x=3\,\text{cm}.$
